newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar eases, bonds jump on CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar eases, bonds jump on CPI data.

text.p: The Australian dollar eased slightly and bonds jumped in immediate reaction to the second quarter inflation report, which came in slightly below median expectations.

The headline CPI fell 0.2 percent for an annual rate of 0.3 percent compared with quarterly median expectations for a 0.1 percent fall. The underlying rate rose 0.3 percent for an annual 1.7 percent. Forecasts had centred on a 0.4 percent rise.

The dollar was US$0.7367/72 compared with US$0.7372/77 just before the data release while the September 10-year bond futures contract was 93.595 against a pre-data 93.555. September bill futures also rose, moving to 94.96 from 94.92.
